'''Boris Rozovsky''' is Ford Foundation Professor of Applied Mathematics at [[Brown University]].<ref name="profile">[https://www.dam.brown.edu/people/rozovsky.html Faculty profile], Brown Applied Math., retrieved 2011-05-08.</ref> His research is in [[stochastic analysis]], particularly the study of [[stochastic partial differential equation]]s.

Rozovsky started his studies in art school, but switched to mathematics; he earned a master's degree in 1968 and a Ph.D. in 1973 from [[Moscow State University]]. He moved to the U.S. in 1988; after teaching for fourteen years at the [[University of Southern California]], he joined the Brown University faculty in 2006.<ref name="welcome">[https://brown.edu/Administration/News_Bureau/2006-07/06-016.ps.html#Rozovsky Physical sciences departments welcome 19 new faculty for 2006-07], Brown University, retrieved 2011-05-08.</ref><ref>[https://dynkincollection.library.cornell.edu/sites/default/files/Rozovsky%20(ENG),%20Ithaca,%20N.%20Y.%20,%20April%2022,%202007.pdf], Boris Rozovsky Interview, Dynkin Collection at Cornell University, retrieved 2012-06-20</ref>

Since 1997, he is a Fellow of the [[Institute of Mathematical Statistics]].<ref>[http://imstat.org/awards/honored_fellows.htm#R List of Fellows] {{Webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20161019175343/http://imstat.org/awards/honored_fellows.htm#R |date=2016-10-19 }}, Institute of Mathematical Statistics, retrieved 2011-05-08.</ref>

In 1997, he was awarded the [[Peter-the-Great Medal]].<ref name="profile"/>

In 2003 he was awarded the [[Kolmogorov Medal]].<ref name="profile"/>
